title: Bone marrow biopsy
what: With a thin needle, the doctor takes a small amount of bone marrow, usually from the back of the hip bone, sometimes from the breastbone. It is done with local numbing.
why: To find the cause of changes in blood tests, for blood disorders, or to check treatment.
duration: the procedure itself usually takes 15 to 30 minutes; results usually in a few days to 1 to 2 weeks
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. Your doctor will decide if anything needs to change
If you are scared. Sometimes a calming medicine can be given

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Usually a complete blood count and clotting test are done first.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: You can usually eat, unless sedation is planned. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Someone with you
prepare.text: If you get a calming medicine, it is best to have someone take you home.

bring: Your referral and blood test results
Someone to take you home, if you have sedation
steps: You lie on your side or stomach
The skin over the bone is cleaned and numbed with an injection
The surface of the bone is numbed too
A special needle goes into the bone
A small amount of marrow is drawn into a syringe
Sometimes a tiny core of bone is taken
The needle is removed, and a pressure bandage is put on
feel: A prick and stinging from the numbing
Pressure as the needle goes into the bone
A brief pulling pain while the marrow is drawn, for a few seconds
after: Lie on the puncture site for 10 to 20 minutes
Keep the bandage dry for 24 hours
The spot may ache for 1 to 3 days. Your doctor will suggest a painkiller
A hematologist usually explains the results
red_flags: The bandage soaks through with blood: press on it and tell your doctor
A fever over 38°C (100.4°F), or redness and pus at the puncture site
Severe pain that keeps getting worse

faq.a: The skin and bone are numbed. It is unpleasant for a few seconds while the marrow is drawn.

faq.q: Is it dangerous for the spinal cord?
faq.a: No. Bone marrow and the spinal cord are different things. The sample is taken from the hip bone or breastbone, not the spine.

reminders.text: Bone marrow biopsy tomorrow. Bring your test results and a list of medicines. Eat as the clinic told you.
